extracted.intended_audience: SEO practitioners, link builders, and PR professionals aiming to earn backlinks and topical authority
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for using PR tactics (data-driven releases, targeted pitching, and distribution) to earn high-authority, dofollow backlinks and build topical authority for SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned media = high-authority dofollow backlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media produces high-authority dofollow backlinks that are valuable for SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage that results in direct links from authoritative outlets rather than only syndication or nofollow placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire releases = limited nofollow value
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire releases tend to provide limited SEO value because they are often nofollow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire syndication as an SEO floor (baseline distribution) but not as a primary source of high-value backlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branded mentions count even without links
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of your brand—even without an actual link—can still be beneficial for SEO/brand signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track both linked coverage and branded mentions; leverage mentions to build reputation and future linking opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage clusters create topical authority signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple related coverage items (coverage clusters) help create topical authority signals for your site/brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to brief multiple outlets and produce a set of related pieces so search engines see a cluster of coverage around your topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper step: find topics with existing media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify topics that already have coverage in the press as targets for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing articles as a signal that journalists care about the topic and will consider linking to a superior resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper step: create a substantially better resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a resource that is substantially better than what exists (data, depth, design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements can be original data, deeper analysis, superior visuals/design, or unique formats that make it link-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper step: pitch journalists who covered the inferior version
rubrics_metrics.description: Target journalists who previously covered the weaker piece when pitching your improved resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research prior coverage to personalize outreach and demonstrate why your resource is an upgrade over what they already wrote about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper step: offer a 'newer, better' version they can link to
rubrics_metrics.description: Position your asset as the newer, better resource that the journalist can reference and link to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the pitch around clear improvements and linkage opportunity; make it easy for the journalist to swap or add your link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research / data-driven releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Original research and proprietary data have the highest pickup rate from journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize original studies, surveys, anonymized internal data, or year-over-year proprietary trends as the basis for PR releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey data your industry hasn't seen
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct and release survey data that fills a gap in industry knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-executed surveys with representative samples and clear methodology increase newsworthiness and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal data anonymized and aggregated
rubrics_metrics.description: Use anonymized, aggregated internal data as a source of proprietary insights for releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure privacy and sound aggregation; highlight unique findings that journalists can't get elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-over-year trends with proprietary numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish year-over-year trend data derived from proprietary numbers to demonstrate change or patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend data gives journalists a narrative and context; include clear visuals and concise takeaways.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'State of the X' annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Create annual 'State of' reports (e.g., 'State of X') as recurring flagship assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring reports become expected resources that attract consistent coverage and help build topical authority over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch subject: numbered insight from data study
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject lines should highlight a numbered insight drawn from your data study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, specific subject (e.g., '3 surprising findings on X') increases open rates and signals a clear news hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Para 1: one specific finding that surprises
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph should state one specific, surprising finding to hook the journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the most newsworthy stat or takeaway to capture attention quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Para 2: methodology in one sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Second paragraph should summarize your methodology in one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide credibility quickly—sample size, timeframe, or data source—so journalists can trust and use the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Para 3: offer of full report + interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Third paragraph should offer access to the full report and availability for interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for the reporter to get more information or a spokesperson; offer exclusive angles where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch sign-off: phone, email, calendar link
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign-offs should include phone, email, and a calendar link for easy scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce friction for follow-up by providing direct contact details and a way to book time immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ego bait: quote the journalist or publication in your release
rubrics_metrics.description: Include or reference the journalist or their publication in the release to flatter and engage them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use genuine, relevant quotes or references—avoid spurious flattery; tie the mention to the reporter's prior coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ego bait: mention them in social posts about the release
rubrics_metrics.description: Call out the journalist or publication in social posts promoting your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging them in social can increase visibility and reciprocity, but avoid spammy over-tagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ego bait: offer them first look in exchange for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Give selected journalists a first look at the report in exchange for coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering an exclusive can increase pickup and build relationships; be transparent about exclusivity terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ego bait: tag them appropriately (not spammy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When tagging journalists or outlets, do so appropriately and sparingly to avoid being perceived as spam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate handles, relevant context, and limit tags to those directly relevant to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution hierarchy for link value
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize distribution by outlet authority and topical fit: Tier 1 outlets → industry trade publications → niche blogs → wire syndication for SEO floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chase Tier 1 for highest authority links, use trade pubs to build topical relevance, engage niche blogs for engaged audiences, and use wire services as a baseline distribution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid buying coverage (paid links risk penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not buy coverage because Google penalizes paid links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on earned, editorial coverage rather than paid placements that may be harmful for SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reciprocal link arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reciprocal link schemes that exchange links for links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal linking can appear manipulative to search engines and harm long-term SEO integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass cold outreach without research
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't send mass, unpersonalized outreach; research is required for effective pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize based on the journalist's prior work and beat; targeted outreach yields better pickup rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'guest post for link' schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid guest posting solely for links (a manipulative tactic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guest posts should provide real value to the publication's audience; avoid transactional link exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'we have some data' pitches
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't send vague pitches that say only 'we have some data' without a specific hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always lead with a concrete, surprising finding or numerical hook in outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric: Specific numerical hook
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful PR asset should include a specific numerical hook (a clear stat or metric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers make stories more newsworthy—lead with the most compelling statistic and explain its significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric: Personalized to journalist's prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize pitches to the journalist's prior coverage and interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference their past articles to show relevance and reduce the chance the pitch will be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric: Multiple media outlets briefed
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief multiple media outlets to create broader pickup and cluster effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate outreach to create simultaneous or cascading coverage, strengthening topical signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric: Clean, dofollow earned coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for clean, earned coverage that results in dofollow links where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track link attributes; focus resources on opportunities likely to produce editorial (dofollow) links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric: Topical authority cluster created
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure success by whether the campaign creates a cluster of topical coverage that reinforces authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the campaign not just by individual links but by the collection of coverage and how it signals expertise to search engines.
